topic: How does a touchscreen know where you touched?

claims.claim: A capacitive panel is glass coated with a transparent conductor such as ITO.
claims.passage: consists of an insulator, such as glass, coated with a transparent conductor, such as indium tin oxide (ITO)

claims.claim: In mutual capacitance, conductors cross without electrical contact; each crossing forms a capacitor.
claims.passage: the mutual crossing of one electrical conductor with another ... with no direct electrical contact, forms a capacitor

claims.claim: Voltage pulses are applied to the conductors one at a time and couple to every crossing conductor.
claims.passage: High frequency voltage pulses are applied to these conductors, one at a time. These pulses capacitively couple to every conductor that intersects it

claims.claim: The body conducts; a finger changes the local field, reducing capacitance between the crossing conductors.
claims.passage: the human body is also an electrical conductor ... Bringing a finger ... changes the local electrostatic field, which in turn reduces the capacitance between these intersecting conductors

claims.claim: A significant change in sensed signal strength is used to determine the touch location, processed by the controller.
claims.passage: Any significant change in the strength of the signal sensed is used to determine ...; The location is then sent to the controller

guardrails: grid drawn schematically: real pitch is millimetres and line counts are higher
mutual-capacitance design only; other touch technologies exist
